root_cause.text: In `f2fs_write_end_io()`, the superblock structure (`sbi`) is accessed to wake up the checkpoint thread after `folio_end_writeback()` has been called, creating a race condition where a concurrent unmount operation (`kill_f2fs_super()`) can free `sbi` once writeback completes.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff shows that the check `!get_pages(sbi, F2FS_WB_CP_DATA) && wq_has_sleeper(&sbi->cp_wait)` (which accesses `sbi`) was moved from after the folio loop (where `folio_end_writeback(folio)` is called) to inside the loop before `folio_end_writeback(folio)` is executed. The commit message also explains that `kill_f2fs_super()` guarantees all folios end writeback before freeing `sbi`, making it unsafe to access `sbi` after the last `folio_end_writeback()`.
